newsitem.title: DUBAI: Abu Dhabi LPG export volumes to be trimmed - trade.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi LPG export volumes to be trimmed - trade.

text.p: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company's (ADNOC) exports of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) will be capped in December because of operational setbacks at an Abu Dhabi gas field development project, Gulf traders said on Monday.
"ADNOC has found it very difficult to produce LPG at contract volume," one LPG customer based in the UAE said.
Gulf traders said that ADNOC exported some 300,000 tonnes in a typical month but that volumes next month are anticipated to be some 50,000 tonnes below normal.
The lower than anticipated export schedule is linked to commissioning problems a gas liquids expansion project at the onshore Bab field, trade sources said.

"October output of LPG from the (Bab) project is understood to have averaged some 800,000 tonnes a year, less than half the full production target of 1.8 million tonnes a year," the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.
